## 1. Define the Design Deliverable

Produce a compact design with the following fields. Mark unresolved facts and the evidence needed to resolve them; do not replace them with assumed library guarantees.

| Deliverable | Required decision |
| --- | --- |
| Goals and non-goals | User outcome, workload, quality criteria, latency/cost limits, allowed effects, deployment/runtime and intentionally excluded behavior. |
| Execution topology | Each generator, flow, agent, tool and child boundary; who chooses the next step; why a simpler topology is insufficient. |
| Data and provider contracts | Signature inputs/outputs, invariants, media/evidence semantics, chosen providers/models and acceptable fallback substitutes. |
| Context and state ownership | Corpus orientation, run history, retrieval, runtime skills, continuation state and durable business records; tenant scope, persistence and freshness owners. |
| Trust and lifecycle | Authenticated identity, tool authorization/approval, clarification, wake/resume correlation, cancellation, retry safety, uncertain outcomes and output delivery. |
| Operations and improvement | Usage attribution, observability/privacy, pricing, evaluation criteria, improvement mechanism and spending bounds. |
| Implementation and verification plan | Ordered specialist sections to read, interfaces to implement, staged checks and authorization required for billed/live/state-changing work. |

For each material choice, state **requirement → selected mechanism → rejected alternative → consequence → specialist section**. A list of Ax APIs without these reasons is not a design.

## 3. Choose Execution Topology

| Need | Choose | Reject or qualify | Implementation destination |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One typed extraction, decision or generation contract | `ax(...)` / `AxGen` | No agent, RLM or DAG merely to wrap a single contract. A generator can still take several model/tool steps; it is not a one-call guarantee. | [Generators: Construction and execution defaults](gen.md#construction-and-execution-defaults); [Signatures: String syntax and field types](signature.md#string-syntax-and-field-types) |
| Known dependencies, parallel independent work, application-defined branches or map/reduce | `flow(...)` / `AxFlow` with typed nodes and explicit input/output mappings | A DAG does not provide an external event inbox or durable application transactions. Guard feedback loops; do not assume untaken branch results exist. | [Flows: Builder rules and boundaries](flow.md#builder-rules-and-boundaries) and State Evolution |
| Model-directed tool selection, evidence gathering, clarification and synthesis | `agent(...)` / `AxAgent` with scoped functions/native clients | Do not use a decision-only provider as the general actor. Do not treat model-selected actions as authorization. | [Core agents: Choose the Agent Shape](agent.md#choose-the-agent-shape) and Defaults and Execution Constraints |
| Large context requiring code inspection, computed intermediate values or multi-turn code execution | Agent runtime/RLM, `AxJSRuntime`, declared `contextFields` | RLM is an agent execution strategy, not a separate durable workflow engine. Ordinary agent setup remains in the core guide. | [RLM: Mental Model](agent-rlm.md#mental-model) and RLM Actor Code Rules |
| Distinct specialists with their own signatures, tools/runtime or instructions | Explicit children in `functions`, with `agentIdentity` and meaningful namespaces | `llmQuery(...)` is a focused semantic query over narrowed context, not a tool-using child agent. Thread parent fields explicitly. | [Core agents: Child Agents, Identity, and Namespaces](agent.md#child-agents-identity-and-namespaces); [RLM: Use These Defaults](agent-rlm.md#use-these-defaults) |
| Notifications, webhooks, queues, timers or completion events must wake/resume programs | `AxEventRuntime` around the selected generator/agent/flow | Sources and protocol callbacks enqueue or observe; they do not invoke models directly. An explicit route chooses observe/invalidate/wake/resume. | [Event runtime: Rules](event-runtime.md#rules); [MCP: Subscriptions, events, and ownership](mcp.md#subscriptions-events-and-ownership) |

AxAgent runs distiller → executor → responder, but `directResponse: 'auto'` can skip the executor for context-only answers. Static agents without executor authority are respond-only. When tools or native operations exist, direct response is constrained against live-state requests, side effects and listed tool domains. Recommend evaluating tool-required versus direct-answer cases rather than using executor skipping as an application safety boundary. See [RLM: Direct respond](agent-rlm.md#direct-respond-executor-skip).

## 4. Define Data and Provider Contracts Together

**Signature first.** Declare named inputs/outputs, optionality, arrays, constraints and descriptions with signature strings, `s()` or `f()`. Use schemas for shape, `addAssert()` for complete-output invariants and `addStreamingAssert()` for partial-output invariants. Reward scores are selection preferences, not hard validation. `fn()` gives host tools typed arguments/returns; handler authorization remains separate. Read [Signatures](signature.md), [Generators: Validation, selection, and hard guards](gen.md#validation-selection-and-hard-guards) and [Core agents: Tool Functions and Schemas](agent.md#tool-functions-and-schemas).

For external schemas, use the current [Zod-only conversion contract](signature.md#standard-schema-zod), not older “any Standard Schema vendor” examples. Native fields need no Zod installation; input enums cannot become output-only Ax `class` fields.

**Decision versus generation.** Jev, OpenAI Decisions and Gemini Decisions support required flat boolean/class/rubric score outputs; only Jev adds experimental Box. They are not arbitrary numeric, optional/array/nested/freeform or general tool providers. Native APIs differ: Jev supports structured state/criteria, OpenAI uses ordered questions and per-question refusals, and Gemini uses named questions/multimodal blocks with input-only usage and HTTP safety errors. Gemini's native Score limit is 255 levels, not the shared signature limit of 10; its dedicated Developer API is not Vertex or GenerateContent. Compose decisions with a generative provider for prose or a tool-using actor. Native versus elicited provenance does not imply correctness or equal calibration. Read [provider differences](typesafe.md#provider-differences), [evidence](typesafe.md#evidence-provenance-and-reranking) and the chosen native contract before implementation.

**Atomic judgments, host policy.** Separate semantic questions from authoritative lookups/calculations, ordered rules and effect dispatch. Customer claims and model extractions are not system-of-record facts. Use multiple flags for overlapping properties, not one exclusive Choice. Shared-state batches must have no answer dependencies; later answers require later calls. Preserve distinct refusal, uncertainty, inapplicability and unavailable/stale-fact states. Resolve or safely hold uncertain higher-priority rules before lower-priority outcomes. Applicability and selected-label probability need separate gates; confidence is not correctness. Compatibility reports rank providers and report supported/missing capabilities, including independent audio input/output counts; they do not measure semantic quality. For function tools on GPT-6 Sol/Luna or GPT-5.6 Sol, explicitly select `thinkingTokenBudget: 'none'` (or `config.reasoningEffort: 'none'`); this deliberately disables reasoning. Reject Astra/GPT-6.1 Sol Chat tool designs before transport: these models require reasoning and reject function tools on that profile. **Streaming is a presentation protocol, not a commit signal.** Merge deltas per `index`, append strings/arrays, replace other values and reset accumulated output on a new `version`. Validation/refusal retries or processor feedback may replace prior output. Partial JSON repair preserves string contents; do not “fix” partial strings into new literals. A valid-looking partial result can still end in failure. Recommend publishing business effects only through an authorized application action, never from a UI delta. Quality evaluation/content-aware selection is application-owned, not semantic balancing. | [AI providers: Routing And Balancing](ai.md#routing-and-balancing) |
| Streaming fallback | Failover can occur before the first emitted chunk; partial output cannot be transparently replayed after emission. Define UI failure/reset behavior. | [AI providers: Routing And Balancing](ai.md#routing-and-balancing); [Generators: Streaming output and replacement versions](gen.md#streaming-output-and-replacement-versions) |

For `gemini-4-hydrogen`, choose a supported logical thinking level and an explicit output bound within its per-segment limit; do not substitute a numeric thinking budget or assume automatic continuation. See [Hydrogen reasoning and limits](ai.md#gemini-4-hydrogen) and its two [provider fixtures](../examples/04-providers.ts).

**Bedrock schema output and function tools require different choices.** For schema-only generation on verified Bedrock OpenAI Chat Completions models, choose native JSON Schema; complex AxGen signatures use it by default, so do not disable reasoning merely to obtain structured output. For function tools on GPT-6 Sol/Luna or GPT-5.6 Sol, explicitly select `thinkingTokenBudget: 'none'` (or `config.reasoningEffort: 'none'`); this deliberately disables reasoning. Reject Astra/GPT-6.1 Sol Chat tool designs before transport: these models require reasoning and reject function tools on that profile. When both reasoning and tools are required, choose `name: 'openai-responses'` with the same Bedrock base URL rather than a blanket reasoning disable. Choose Standard for the verified Chat models; unsupported Flex/Priority tiers fail locally. Native AWS Converse is a separate transport, not either OpenAI-compatible profile. Implementation: [AI providers: AWS Bedrock](ai.md#aws-bedrock).

**Streaming is a presentation protocol, not a commit signal.** Merge deltas per `index`, append strings/arrays, replace other values and reset accumulated output on a new `version`. Validation/refusal retries or processor feedback may replace prior output. Partial JSON repair preserves string contents; do not “fix” partial strings into new literals. A valid-looking partial result can still end in failure. Recommend publishing business effects only through an authorized application action, never from a UI delta. See [Generators: Streaming output and replacement versions](gen.md#streaming-output-and-replacement-versions).

Text accompanying tool-call chunks also belongs to replay history even when that chunk does not trigger field extraction; presentation and next-request history need separate checks. See `03-tools-streaming/mixed-tool-text-history` in the [streaming module](../examples/03-tools-streaming.ts).

**Document attribution is not answer verification.** Preserve native passage/source associations and their matching request; a citation can identify supplied evidence without proving that the answer follows from it or that the source is true. Choose a text contract when native Anthropic citations are required: enabled citations reject provider-native structured JSON, and document indices are request-local. Use [document source/citation rules](ai.md#anthropic-document-citations), then [generation logs/usage](gen.md#normalized-chat-logs-and-usage) only when consuming passage associations. Select one [document fixture](../examples/37-document-citations.ts) through the [index](../examples/INDEX.md#exact-release-and-source-backed-cases).

**Refusal recovery separates model history from presentation.** A refusal retry drops the refused assistant turn, even after partial streaming, and resumes from the same user or function-result message. That prevents refused content from contaminating the retry prompt; the application must still reset provisional UI output on a new version. It does not authorize replaying completed external effects. Read [Generators: Errors and strict labels](gen.md#errors-and-strict-labels).

**Protocol-complete tool outcomes are not execution authority.** AxGen answers an unknown function name with a per-call error while retaining valid sibling results, so the next model request has every call ID answered and can correct the name. [PR 878](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/878) introduced the TypeScript behavior; 25.4.9 [PR 883](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/883) aligns generated Python, Java, C++, Go and Rust forward/streaming recovery with its plain error text and result-formatter bypass. This does not grant permission, make effects idempotent or assign replay ownership: authorization, deduplication and any deliberate replay remain application responsibilities. It is not an agent/RLM or universal generated-language parity claim. Read [Generators: Function calling and stop functions](gen.md#function-calling-and-stop-functions).

**Visible output and replay history are separate contracts.** Hiding displayed thoughts does not remove signed/redacted thinking retained for provider replay. Recommend treating that history as sensitive protocol state, with explicit access, logging and retention policies rather than rewriting signed blocks to implement a display policy. Preserve required block order, signatures and opaque data. For Anthropic replay, empty visible text must not manufacture a text block; cache markers belong only on eligible text/tool-use blocks, never signed/redacted thinking. [PR 876](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/876) fixes the TypeScript empty-text case; [PR 883](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/pull/883) closes the named generated replay/cache-boundary gap, not unrelated provider parity. Read [AI providers: Anthropic Model-Specific Behavior](ai.md#anthropic-model-specific-behavior) and [Context Caching](ai.md#context-caching).

**Cache creation is an instruction-policy boundary.** Gemini caches retain the system instructions captured at creation; define immutable creation policy and recreate caches when that policy changes. The 25.4.4 prefix/breakpoint fix preserves every ordered system message on either side of the content breakpoint. Upgrading does not repair existing cached instructions: expire or recreate affected caches before relying on the corrected policy. Read [AI providers: Gemini system instructions and cache migration](ai.md#gemini-system-instructions-and-cache-migration).

## Evidence, provenance, and reranking

Jev, OpenAI Decisions, Gemini Decisions, and generative providers support decision metadata through signature fields:

```text
query:string, document:string ->
  relevant:boolean(evidence, threshold 0.7),
  category:class "support, billing"(evidence),
  relevance:score "Irrelevant, Related, Partial answer, Direct answer"(evidence)
```

| Evidence | Fields |
|---|---|
| Boolean | `value`, `probability`, `threshold`, `provenance` |
| Class | `value`, complete label-to-probability map, `provenance` |
| Score | Continuous `value` from zero to final rubric index, ordered `levels`, ordered `probabilities`, `provenance` |

Native boolean/class/score results may also contain provider `confidence` when supplied (Jev Noul has none). Scores without `(evidence)` return only numeric values; existing scalar boolean/class behavior is unchanged.

Ax preserves transported native selected classes, continuous scores, probabilities, and confidence rather than recomputing them. TypeSafe documents live Choice as the highest-probability label and Score as the probability-weighted rubric index; Google and OpenAI likewise document top-choice/expected-index semantics. Synthetic fixtures deliberately supplying a different selection or score test SDK preservation, not expected inference semantics. For generative models Ax requests probabilities, derives boolean/class locally, and computes score as `sum(index * probability) / sum(probability)`. Stored probabilities remain unchanged; Ax never invents confidence.

Ax—not generated output—sets `provenance.source` (`native` or `elicited`), `provider`, and model identity. Jev/OpenAI use the response model; Gemini returns none, so Ax uses the requested model. Shared result shapes do not imply equally calibrated probabilities/confidence across providers/models. Evaluate thresholds/ranking on your data. Rubric scores are not probabilities of correctness.

For reranking, judge every query/document pair, retain application candidate IDs, and sort by `relevance.value` within one rubric/model. Processors, assertions, result selection, traces, and caches receive decoded results; streaming waits for complete evidence.

```typescript
const judge = ax(f().input('query', f.string()).input('document', f.string())
  .output('relevance', f.score(['Irrelevant', 'Related', 'Partial answer', 'Direct answer']).withEvidence())

## Native questions and application decisions

```typescript
import { typesafe } from '@ax-llm/ax';

const apiKey = process.env.TYPESAFE_API_KEY ?? process.env.TYPESAFE_APIKEY;
if (!apiKey) throw new Error('Set a Typesafe API key.');
const client = typesafe({ apiKey });
const result = await client.systemOne({
  state: { ticket: 'Checkout fails for every customer.', recentEvents: [] },
  questions: {
    urgent: {
      type: 'noul',
      instructions: 'Does this require immediate incident response?',
      criteria: {
        true: { description: 'Core task blocked', examples: ['Cannot pay'] },
        false: 'Routine request or minor inconvenience',
      },
    },
    team: {
      type: 'choice',
      instructions: 'Which team should investigate?',
      criteria: {
        support: 'Product usage questions',
        engineering: 'Broken functionality or service outages',
      },
    },
    severity: {
      type: 'score',
      instructions: 'How severe is the customer impact?',
      criteria: ['Minor inconvenience', 'Feature impaired', 'Core task blocked'],
    },
  },
});
const escalate = result.answers.urgent.noul >= 0.9;
const team = result.answers.team.choice; // 'support' | 'engineering'
const severity = result.answers.severity.score; // Fractional values allowed, 0–2.
const severityOnTen = (severity / 2) * 10; // Explicit application scale.
const models = await client.listModels();
```

Keep questions inline or use `as const satisfies AxAITypesafeQuestions` for reusable definitions to preserve literal question keys/Choice labels.

- Noul returns `noul` in `[0, 1]`, with no separate confidence. Adapter `trueThreshold` does not apply to native clients.
- Choice returns `choice`, `probabilities`, `confidence`; Score returns `score`, `probabilities`, `legend`, `confidence`.
- Responses also include `model` and `usage.input_tokens`/`usage.output_tokens`.
- Choice/Score probabilities must be finite `[0, 1]` values matching criteria keys, summing to one within inclusive `0.01` tolerance. Totals `0.99` and `1.01` are accepted with floating-point summation allowance. Ax preserves probabilities without renormalizing.
- State, instructions, and individual criteria accept text, JSON objects, arrays, or `null`. Nested JSON accepts finite numbers/booleans; bare numbers/booleans are invalid top-level entries. Instructions are optional in Ax/native types, but provide explicit questions: keys identify answers, not instructions. Choice permits 1–255 labels; Score requires 2–10 ordered levels. `null` leaves outcomes undescribed.

Question design:
- Noul asks one clear yes/no judgment; near `0.5` means uncertainty about that judgment, not degree/severity. Use Score for degree. Overlapping flags require separate Nouls composed in code; Choice selects one exclusive outcome.
- Give similar Choice labels distinct descriptions; use an application-valid catch-all or companion applicability gate when the options do not cover all inputs.
- For a selected-label action inspect `probabilities[choice]`. Jev Choice confidence transforms the maximum probability for a fixed option count; it is not independent evidence. For a level-specific Score action inspect that level's probability: equal mean scores can conceal different distributions.
- Use one dimension per Score rubric and describe each level independently, without relying on “more than the previous level.” Preserve fractional zero-based position; explicitly choose rounding, normalization, and weighting in code.
- All questions share state. Group by relevant context and identify source paths. Structured instruction fields are application-defined; simple strings remain the default. Same-request questions cannot consume another answer; dependencies require later calls.
- Evaluate held-out representative inputs plus adversarial/irrelevant state, negation, boundaries and option-order changes. Higher confidence after a rewrite does not prove greater accuracy; confidence describes a distribution, not correctness.

Provider guidance: [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul), [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice), [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score), [official API types](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/main/src/types.ts).

## Atomic judgments and host policy

Jev supplies semantic judgments; code owns authoritative facts/calculations, ordered rules and effects. Keep Choice/Score and Ax decision APIs for their typed contracts, but do not bury an entire business policy in one Choice. Model-extracted values and customer claims are not system-of-record facts: verify eligibility, balances, amounts, identity and current status against authenticated records, and calculate exact comparisons in code.

- Send bounded, relevant structured context with explicit source/field paths; separate customer assertions from verified records. Batch narrow, answer-independent questions over that context. “Independent” means no answer dependencies, not statistical independence, invariance after edits or a calibration guarantee. Questions needing another answer require a later call.
- Retain raw Noul probabilities through native answers or boolean evidence. Define a host-owned three-valued policy: yes above an evaluated upper boundary, no below a lower boundary, uncertain between them, with explicit inclusive/exclusive boundaries. A scalar boolean alone cannot retain that uncertainty. Missing required facts also need an explicit unresolved outcome.
- Evaluate multi-intent rules in priority order. For example: unauthorized-charge report → human/legal request → eligible refund → retention → ordinary answer. An uncertain higher-priority rule must trigger review, clarification or a defined safe hold before any lower-priority outcome; do not silently treat uncertainty as false. Dispatch authorized effects only after policy selection, separately from judgments and explanations.
- Optional applicability gate: pair a forced Choice with a companion Noul asking whether any supplied option applies. Ignore the Choice when inapplicable; preserve review when applicability is uncertain. Independently gate the selected label's probability even when applicability is high: “some option applies” does not establish which one. Choice confidence alone establishes neither applicability nor correctness. Likewise, pair Box with a presence judgment and ignore its region unless presence passes policy.
- Optional speculative fan-out: ask answer-independent questions together even when only some branches will matter, then ignore irrelevant answers in code. Never let an irrelevant answer override a selected branch or authorize an effect.
- Optional composite scoring: use one Score rubric per dimension, normalize each by its own final rubric index, and apply explicit application weights in code. Preserve component scores/distributions. A weighted aggregate is an application score, not a joint-event probability; multiplying judgments does not establish one either.
- Keep privacy-aware traces with available model identity, question IDs/versions, raw probabilities, threshold/policy versions, evaluated rule IDs/order, selected/blocked outcome and fact source IDs/versions. Redact/minimize payloads and control access/retention; do not invent unavailable identities or log secrets to obtain observability.
- After changing wording, context, model, thresholds, rules or facts contracts, run targeted evaluation on representative labeled cases: uncertain boundaries, overlapping intents, missing/stale facts, inapplicable Choice, absent Box targets and effect denial. Re-evaluate affected judgments and end-to-end policy; no automatic correctness or calibration follows from decomposition.
- Keep refusal, semantic uncertainty, inapplicability and missing/stale authoritative facts as distinct states. A refused judgment is not a low probability; unavailable facts are not negative semantic answers. Route each through explicit host policy.

Read [Don’t Call It a Decision Model](https://typesafe.ai/blog/dont-call-it-a-decision-model), [how to build with System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one), [confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence), and TypeSafe [patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns) for [probability routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/probability-routing), [speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out) and [composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring). Treat thresholds as workload-specific policies, not portable error-rate guarantees.

Selected examples: [26 architecture](../examples/26-architecture.ts), `26-architecture/evidence-aware-ticket`; [06 decisions](../examples/06-decisions.ts), `06-decisions/threshold-ownership` and `06-decisions/applicability-gate`. Read the architecture case for ordered host policy, then the decision cases for threshold ownership and applicability.

## Models, transport, and diagnostics

| Setting | Signature provider | Native client |
|---|---|---|
| Default model override | `config: { model: 'jev-latest' }` | `model: 'jev-latest'` |
| Per-call model override | Third `forward()` argument `{ model }` | `systemOne({ state, questions, model })` |
| Endpoint | `apiURL`, default `https://api.typesafe.ai` | Same |
| Authentication | `apiKey` or `credentialProvider` | Same; optional static `headers` |
| Transport | `options.fetch`, `timeout`, `retry`, `abortSignal` | Same; methods take a second transport-options argument, or first for `listModels()` |

`listModels()` returns native cards (`name`, `description`, `release_date`), not changes to configured Ax model aliases. Renewable credential callbacks receive `{ profile, operation, method, url }` on each attempt; operation is `chat` for inference and `models` for discovery. Native instance/per-call cancellation signals both apply.

Context limits cover combined state/instructions/criteria; consult [models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models). Ax neither silently truncates nor claims exact local token counts. Token usage is returned; Ax assumes no model token prices.

Adapter diagnostics use `program.getUsage()`/`program.getChatLog()`. Logs retain `providerMetadata.typesafe.answers`; direct `.chat()` responses retain the same metadata. Native calls return usage/full answers directly. No generic metadata getter or alternate forward result is needed.

## Routing and hybrid workflows

Typesafe-only balancers preserve schema-required generation for scalar signatures. Mixed pools retain normal prompting; Typesafe is eligible only if the actual request already contains a supported output schema. Incompatible requests are excluded from selection/fallbacks even with degradation enabled. Bare chat without a supported schema fails.

For prose, call a second `ax()` with a generative provider and pass explicit inputs. Ax does not automatically split `urgent:boolean, reply:string`. The architecture case passes only ticket ID and selected outcome: its prose is an outcome acknowledgement, not a guaranteed factual rationale. An evidence-based explanation would need an explicit evidence/facts handoff and separate evaluation. Agents requiring tools/code generation use a generative actor and a separate decision step; see [Agent](agent.md).

## Runnable examples and live checks

Local offline contracts: [`06-decisions`](../examples/06-decisions.ts), cases `adapter-values`, `adapter-evidence`, `native-structured`, `native-validation`, `reranking`, `typed-generation-handoff`, and `refusal-policy`; image transport and presence gates: [`07-images`](../examples/07-images.ts), cases `native-localization`, `native-assets`, `generative-localization`, and `validation-and-absence`. Gemini contracts use `06-decisions/google-gemini-decisions-evidence`, `06-decisions/google-gemini-native-multimodal`, and `06-decisions/google-gemini-native-validation`. Injected HTTP answers establish SDK contracts, not inference quality or calibration.

Run in the Ax repository root; `tsx` loads `.env`:

```bash
npm run tsx src/examples/typescript/generation/typesafe.ts
npm run tsx src/examples/typescript/generation/typesafe-native.ts
npm run tsx src/examples/typescript/generation/typesafe-hybrid.ts
npm run tsx src/examples/typescript/generation/value-descriptions.ts
```

First two require `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `TYPESAFE_APIKEY`; last two also require `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_APIKEY`. [Comparison](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/main/src/examples/typescript/generation/value-descriptions.ts) uses the same described signature across providers; [native](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/main/src/examples/typescript/generation/typesafe-native.ts) covers all primitives/model discovery; [hybrid](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/main/src/examples/typescript/generation/typesafe-hybrid.ts) composes two programs. Assert response contracts in live checks, never exact model probabilities.

## Provider differences

Shared evidence shapes do not equate native APIs, probability semantics, calibration or refusal behavior.

| Contract | Typesafe / Jev | OpenAI Decisions | Gemini Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Endpoint / auth | `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`; API key or renewable credentials | `https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions`; bearer key or renewable credentials | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/decisions`; `x-goog-api-key` or renewable credentials |
| Native input / questions | Structured `state`; named Noul/Choice/Score/Box map | Text/user inline-image messages in Ax 25.4.10; ordered predicate/choice/score array | Text or multimodal blocks; named Noul/Choice/Score map |
| Evidence / refusal | Native answers; Noul has no confidence; no declared refusal variant | Native answers and per-question refusal union | Native answers with required confidence, including Noul; safety blocks are HTTP errors |
| Media | Experimental PNG/JPEG and Box under limits above | Ax 25.4.10 client: inline images; no Box/audio/files | Image/audio plus PDF/image/audio/video files; no Box |
| Usage / limits | Input/output tokens; native Choice 1–255, Score 2–10 | Full usage; Choice 2–255, Score 2–10 | Per-modality input usage, zero output tokens; native Choice/Score 2–255, signature Score 2–10 |
| Execution limits | No prose/tools/token stream; see adapter restrictions | No prose/tools/token stream; [OpenAI contract](ai.md#openai-decisions) | Developer API only; no Vertex, prose/tools/token stream/cache/thinking/Flex/Priority |

## Defaults and Execution Constraints

- Use `agent(...)`, not `new AxAgent(...)`, for new code.
- Prefer string signatures or `f()` signatures to hand-written signature objects, and `fn(...)` host functions to hand-written JSON Schema.
- `ai` supplies instance defaults; delegated child calls receive the caller's runtime AI. For a distinct child model, set `contextOptions: { ai: childAI }`, `executorOptions: { ai: childAI }`, and `responderOptions: { ai: childAI }`. Use `judgeAI` for the default judge/teacher and `agentIdentity` for child metadata.
- Prefer namespaced functions, e.g. `utils.search(...)` and `kb.find(...)`.
- Delegate through explicit child agents in `functions`, not recursive `llmQuery(...)`.
- Actor responses must contain one executable program. Multiple fenced code blocks reject the entire turn without executing any block; the runtime asks for one program. This applies to text and structured JSON responses, with LF or CRLF line endings.
- Actor code stages require structured generation with the exact `javascriptCode` wire key. Native-capable providers retain strict `json_schema`; providers such as DeepSeek use validated `json_object` and need no provider-visible tools for runtime execution.
- Upstream reports `validation_retries` with one correction attempt by default for generated Go, Python, Java, C++, and Rust actor stages (`0` fails immediately). These generated-package contracts are not verified by the TypeScript package; check the target release before using them.
- Do not combine actor `console.log(...)` with `final(...)`.

### Direct-response default

`directResponse` defaults to `'auto'`. If no executor authority is needed, the distiller ends with `respond(task, evidence)` and skips the executor: zero executor model calls. Static agents with no functions, child agents, or native MCP/UCP operations are always respond-only. Agents with any such authority retain the executor and permit `respond` only under a conservative covenant: no live/fresh-state requests, no side effects, and nothing covered by a listed function/module domain. Set `directResponse: 'off'` to always run the executor. This distiller shortcut does not replace the host-function `final(...)` protocol below.

## Event-Triggered Flows

An AxFlow is an `AxProgrammable` event target. The runtime maps an event into
the Flow's typed initial state and propagates `eventContext`, cancellation, and
idempotency metadata to every node. Abandoned branches still use normal Flow
cancellation semantics.

Task-backed MCP tools called by a Flow node register a continuation on the
shared event context. `axMCPEventRoutes` observes progress and resumes the Flow
on input-required or terminal task notifications.

For resource-driven wake, discover the endpoint with `inspectCatalog()` and
give `AxMCPEventSource` an explicit `resourceSubscriptions` policy. Managed
subscriptions reconcile list changes and reconnect separately from the Flow;
subscription alone never starts or resumes a Flow.

UCP lifecycle webhooks use the same continuation boundary through
`AxUCPWebhookEventSource`. Correlate on `ucp.checkout` or `ucp.order` only after
the signed request has been verified and mapped to application identity.

Use `eventTarget('id').program(flow).wakeInput(...).resumeInput(...)` when wake
and resume events have different shapes. Segment-safe `eventPath` mappings are
validated against the Flow signature before any node executes; a declarative
`.waitFor(kind, path)` creates the owned continuation consumed by the resume
route.

Reusable `eventInput()` plans are the preferred callback-free boundary.
Callback `mapInput` is normalized against the Flow signature before any node
runs. In generated hosts, immediate publications dispatch inline; the host uses
`nextDueAt()` and `runDue()` for delayed retries, debounce, and continuation
expiry.

## Automatic sessions (TypeScript)

Pass `{ control: runControl() }` to `forward()`. Each node receives its own `root/<nodeName>` scope and conversation. Target that path to restrict an update; root updates also apply to future nodes. Completed nodes are not rerun and controller-attached runs bypass result caching.

The standalone [automatic-session control case](../examples/16-flow.ts) verifies node-targeted versus root updates, separate conversations, completed-node preservation, cache bypass and session cleanup. Its provider-session events are explicit fixtures, not live transport or model-compliance qualification.


Runnable TypeScript examples under `src/examples/typescript/flows/`:

- `astra-parallel-tools.ts`: independent background lookups with isolated node results and automatic parallel scheduling.
- `astra-targeted-control.ts`: steering and reasoning changes scoped to a review node, preserving the completed baseline.
- `astra-cancel-pending.ts`: cancellation while both branches have host tools pending; the example verifies rejection rather than successful completion.

Deterministic coverage lives in `src/ax/flow/flow.sessions.test.ts`, including both automatic and explicit parallel execution, delayed results, active/future root updates, targeted updates, cache bypass, cancellation, and chat-only provider fallback. These session examples and tests are TypeScript-only.

Python, Go, Java, C++, and Rust dispatch independent Core-planned nodes through
owned client and program workers. Built-in providers, routers, and balancers
provide the capability automatically; unsupported custom implementations run the
group serially and emit a `flow_parallel_fallback` trace. Each node owns its
conversation, pending calls, and control path; successful results merge in plan
order. Native tests and provider-backed `flows/astra_parallel` examples cover
coordinated overlap. Full session acceptance remains tracked in the AxIR backlog.

## MCP Adapter

Use [MCP](mcp.md) for client construction, transports, authentication, catalogs, subscriptions, tasks, and protocol-specific security policy. This reference owns generic inbox, routing, continuation, store, and sink behavior.

Use `client.inspectCatalog()` to discover server-owned tools, prompts, concrete
resources, and URI templates from only the endpoint. Then use
`AxMCPEventSource({ client, resourceSubscriptions, identity, trust })` with an
explicit none/all/URI/selector policy. Omitted policy subscribes to no
resources. Templates are never expanded automatically. Managed sources diff
catalog changes, restore current logical ownership on reconnect, and release
only their own subscriptions on close. Identity must come from the
application's authenticated client or token mapping; a bare MCP session is
anonymous. Add `...axMCPEventRoutes({ client })` for catalog invalidation,
progress/log observation, and task resume. Resource notifications never get an
implicit wake route. Upstream subscription policy resource: [MCP subscription lifecycle](https://github.com/ax-llm/ax/blob/007ab8366e5bfa98d871feb1af188cc029295c58/docs/MCP_SUBSCRIPTIONS.md).

## UCP Adapter

Use `AxUCPWebhookEventSource({ client, identity })` inside an application-owned
HTTP handler, then call `source.ingest(request)`. The client verifies signer
profile, RFC 9421 signature, digest, freshness and key rotation before enqueue.
Resolve tenant/account identity from trusted application registration after
verification; never copy authority from the business payload.

**25.4.11 replay qualification:** `AxUCPClient.verifyOrderEvent` creates a new
signature verifier per request; its persistent process-local replay check uses
`Webhook-Id`, while that header and `Webhook-Timestamp` need not be signed.
Bind them to the signed `request-id` and `created` before ingestion, and require
the signed signer-profile header. Parse exactly one verified signature member
with unique parameters; bind metadata to that member, not a separately selected
or ambiguous `Signature-Input` entry. The
[`35-ucp/webhook-freshness-member-binding`](../examples/35-ucp.ts) case includes a
fresh `created`-last control and rejects old or ambiguous metadata before enqueue.
The [verified webhook example](../examples/35-ucp.ts) also covers real client
verification, key rotation, tamper/replay rejection and host-bound tenant routing.
Its volatile replay state is not restart durability; production hosts need
durable replay/idempotency policy. Source:
[`25.4.11 client and signing code`](https://unpkg.com/@ax-llm/ax@25.4.11/index.js.map),
embedded `../ucp/client.ts` (`verifyOrderEvent`) and `../ucp/signing.ts`.

Native UCP attachment is independent of transport. The same example carries
UCP through Flow → Agent/Gen and preserves structured results; MCP-backed UCP
also reuses protocol sessions and propagates cancellation. Attaching a client
does not itself authorize purchases or establish tenant isolation.

The generated-language statements below describe the supplied source's scope, not runtime qualification performed by this collection.

Generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust packages expose the same Core-owned
single-worker event state machine plus functioning inline lifecycle dispatch,
continuations, state restoration, cancellation, persisted outputs, isolated
sink redrive, signature-aware path/input/target/route builders, and host-owned
source, sink, clock, and store boundaries. Generated targets use the host
signature plus a typed invocation callback when no common object-safe program
interface exists. Do not claim persistent multi-worker support from
`axevent.single-worker` alone.

Generated runtimes do not create worker threads. `publish()` drains work due at
`clock.now()`. Hosts use `nextDueAt()` to schedule `runDue()` for debounce,
retry, and continuation expiry; `redrive()` is due immediately. Manual clocks
make these transitions deterministic. Generated in-memory stores enforce
10,000 pending deliveries, 64 MiB queued data, 1 MiB per envelope, and a
five-second publication wait.

System and manual clock sleeps accept the generated cancellation token (Go uses
`context.Context`). Cancellation wakes the sleep without advancing a manual
clock, preserves the token's first reason, and removes its wake subscription on
both cancellation and normal completion. Repeated completed sleeps must not
retain timers, callbacks, condition registrations, or manual-clock waiters.
